title: Retrieval metrics
summary: Rank metrics score a retriever against labelled relevant documents: precision@k, recall@k, hit rate, MRR and nDCG. Pick by label type and by whether one chunk or several are needed, and tie k to the chunks your prompt really receives.
useIf: You are choosing or tuning a retriever, reranker or chunking strategy and have, or can build, relevance labels.
avoidIf: You want to know whether the final answer is good. Retrieval metrics say nothing about generation.

explain.md: A **relevance judgment set** (qrels) lists, per query, which documents are relevant, binary or graded. Then, for the top k results:

items: **Precision@k**: relevant results in the top k divided by k. It needs no count of relevant documents but is the least stable standard measure: with only 8 relevant documents a perfect system scores at most 0.4 at k=20 [[r25]].
**Recall@k**: relevant results in the top k divided by all relevant documents. It shows whether the evidence reached the prompt.
**Hit rate@k**: share of queries with at least one relevant result in the top k. This is a conventional definition. No vendor evaluator page checked on 2026-10-13 defines it as a named evaluator.
**MRR**: mean of 1/rank of the first relevant result. Ranks 1, 3, none and 2 give (1 + 0.333 + 0 + 0.5) / 4 = 0.458 [[tr10]].
**nDCG@k**: for graded relevance, discounts gain by log2 of the rank and divides by the best possible ordering [[r25]].

explain.title: nDCG@k
explain.expr: nDCG@k = DCG@k / IDCG@k, with DCG@k = sum over i=1..k of gain(rel_i) / log2(i + 1)
explain.example: Relevance 3, 2, 0, 1 scores 0.985 with linear gain and 0.993 with exponential gain. Libraries differ, so never compare scores across tools without checking [[r46]].

explain.md: Foundry's Document Retrieval evaluator (`builtin.document_retrieval`) reports `ndcg@3`, `xdcg@3`, `fidelity`, `top1_relevance`, `top3_max_relevance`, `holes` and `holes_ratio`. It takes `retrieval_ground_truth` (document_id plus `query_relevance_label`) and `retrieved_documents`, with the label range defaulting to 0 to 4 [[r4]]. **Holes** are retrieved documents that have no judgment, and they distort rank metrics, so watch `holes_ratio`. BEIR spans 18 public datasets, and BM25 is a strong baseline [[r42]].

explain.title: Pick the retrieval metric
explain.prompt: Flip the label type and the answer need. The ranking updates.

options.name: Hit rate and MRR
options.summary: How early the first right chunk appears.

options.name: Recall@k
options.summary: Did the evidence reach the prompt?

options.name: Precision@k
options.summary: Share of the top k that is relevant.

graded.why: Works on a binary cut, ignores grades.

binary.why: Fits one right answer per query.

one.why: FAQ lookup cares about the first hit.

many.why: Ignores the second and third chunk.

binary.why: Reduces to a rank-aware binary score.

many.why: Rewards good ordering of many chunks.

explain.takeaway: Labels decide the family. The evidence your prompt needs decides the member.

whereToUse: Comparing BM25, dense and hybrid retrieval, or two embedding models
Tuning chunk size and overlap before touching the prompt
Measuring a reranker's lift in nDCG and recall at the real k
Regression gates after an index or schema change

use: Labels exist or can be pooled for a query set
Retrieval and generation must be scored separately
k equals the number of chunks the prompt receives
avoid: Using a single k=10 by habit when the prompt gets 4 chunks
Comparing nDCG across libraries without checking the gain formula
Treating high retrieval scores as proof the answer is right
flips: No labels: use judged context metrics and start labelling a small set
Graded relevance exists: prefer nDCG over precision
Several documents must be combined: weight recall@k more than MRR

pitfalls.symptom: nDCG differs between two tools for the same run
pitfalls.cause: Linear versus exponential gain, or a different log base or cutoff
pitfalls.fix: Fix one implementation, record its formula and re-baseline when you change it

pitfalls.symptom: Recall looks fine but answers lack detail
pitfalls.cause: k in the metric is larger than the chunks actually sent to the prompt
pitfalls.fix: Set k to the prompt's real chunk count and report recall at that k

pitfalls.symptom: Scores swing when you add new retrieved documents
pitfalls.cause: Unjudged documents count as non-relevant, so holes distort the metric
pitfalls.fix: Track `holes_ratio`, judge the top results of every system and pool them

scenarios.title: FAQ lookup, one right answer
scenarios.situation: A help-centre assistant answers from a corpus where each question maps to one article. Binary labels exist for 400 queries. The prompt receives three chunks.
unknowns: How often is the right article unlabelled?
scenarios.question: Which metrics do you gate on?

options.name: Hit rate@3 and MRR
options.why: One right chunk is enough and both metrics reward finding it early at the real k.
options.tradeoff: They ignore the second and third chunk, so they hide poor filler context.

options.name: Precision@10
options.why: With one relevant article the score is capped at 0.1 and k does not match the prompt.
options.tradeoff: Precision suits result pages where several relevant items are expected.

options.name: nDCG@3
options.why: Rank aware and fine for binary labels.
options.tradeoff: Harder to explain, and adds little when grades do not exist.

flips.then: Add recall@k at the prompt's chunk count.
Use judged context metrics while labelling.

scenarios.takeaway: One right chunk points to hit rate and MRR at the real k.

scenarios.title: Research assistant, graded evidence
scenarios.situation: An assistant answers analyst questions by synthesising four to six passages from a large archive. Experts graded relevance from 0 to 4 on 150 queries. The prompt receives eight chunks.
unknowns: How many relevant passages does a typical query have?
scenarios.question: Which retrieval metrics and settings do you choose?

options.name: nDCG@8 plus recall@8, with holes_ratio tracked
options.why: Graded labels suit nDCG, coverage needs recall, and holes show where judgments are missing.
options.tradeoff: Two numbers to explain, and labelling must keep pace with new documents.

options.name: MRR only
options.why: It scores only the first relevant passage while the task needs several.
options.tradeoff: MRR is right when one passage answers the question.

options.name: Judged context metrics only
options.tradeoff: Noisier, and it ignores graded labels you already paid for.

flips.then: Judge the top results of each system and pool them before trusting the numbers.

scenarios.takeaway: Graded labels and multi-document answers point to nDCG and recall.

quiz.q: Four queries have the first relevant result at ranks 1, 3, none (not retrieved) and 2. What is MRR to three decimals?
quiz.explain: (1 + 0.333 + 0 + 0.5) / 4 = 0.458. A query with no relevant result contributes 0.

quiz.q: A query has 8 relevant documents. A perfect retriever is scored at k=20. What is the maximum precision@20?
quiz.explain: At most 8 of the 20 results can be relevant, so 8/20 = 0.4. Precision depends on how many relevant documents exist, which is why it is unstable across queries.

quiz.q: A retrieval evaluator reports holes_ratio = 0.35 after you add a new retriever. What does it mean?
options: 35% of retrieved documents have no relevance judgment, so rank metrics are distorted
The judge disagrees with humans 35% of the time
quiz.explain: Holes are retrieved documents with no judgment. Unjudged items are usually counted as non-relevant, which understates the new retriever.

flashcards.back: Mean over queries of 1 divided by the rank of the first relevant result. Ranks 1, 3, none, 2 give 0.458.
It depends on how many relevant documents exist per query. With 8 relevant, a perfect system scores at most 0.4 at k=20.

flashcards.front: Why is nDCG not one number across tools?
flashcards.back: Linear gain uses rel_i, exponential gain uses 2^rel_i - 1. The same ranking can score 0.985 or 0.993.

flashcards.front: What are holes in Foundry's Document Retrieval evaluator?
flashcards.back: Retrieved documents with no relevance judgment. Track holes_ratio because unjudged documents distort rank metrics.
